title: Length-hybridization batcher: KV heat-shedding and GPU defragmentation
creator: Mira Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce p95 generation latency and GPU memory pressure for mixed prompt/response workloads by introducing a length-hybridization scheduling layer that performs KV heat-shedding and periodic GPU slab defragmentation without violating SLOs.

Context: Production traffic shows a bimodal length distribution: short prompts with long responses (assistant-heavy) and long prompts with short completions (prompt-heavy). Current continuous-batcher tends to either over-reserve KV residency for long-turns or excessively evict helpful prefixes, causing cache churn and memory fragmentation on multi-tenant GPUs. This ticket explores a middle-layer that dynamically hybridizes long/short streams into compact execution slots and triggers low-impact defragmentation and KV shedding during low-latency windows.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for mixed-length test harness decreases by >= 8% compared to baseline
GPU active memory fragmentation (measured via slab utilization) reduced by >= 10% across benchmarks
KV hit-rate loss during shedding < 3% for representative prompt sets
No regressions on tail latency for latency-sensitive routes (test route v-blue)
design_decisions: Introduce a lightweight hybridizer that maintains two micro-queues (short-turn and long-turn) and probabilistically interleaves them based on current KV pressure and recent latency signals

KV heat-shedding scoring: combine use-frequency, recency, and token-cost to compute a shedding rank. Lowest-ranked segments are marked for ephemeral eviction with a soft TTL (200-800ms) before hard eviction

GPU defragmentation: perform asynchronous slab compaction during measured low-util windows (observability flags), using incremental copy+free to avoid host stalls rather than a full stop-the-world defrag
Backoff policy: scheduler backs off shedding if upstream client reports >2% degradation in acceptance tests or if request queueing exceeds configured latency headroom
No hard changes to user-visible API; configuration exposed as runtime flags and a console knob under runtime-1.22 for early access

experiments: Exp-01: Baseline continuous-batcher with existing KV eviction (A/B vs hybridizer). Result: hybridizer reduced average KV churn by 14% in mixed suites
Exp-02: KV heat-shedding thresholds sweep [100ms,200ms,500ms,800ms]. Observation: 200-400ms window hits best trade-off between hit-rate and memory relief

Exp-03: Defrag cadence test (every 30s vs 120s vs on-demand). Observation: short cadence (30s) caused minor CPU jitter; 90s cadence with incremental moves gave best slab compaction with <1% request slowdowns
Exp-04: Load spike safety: applied 3x traffic spike. Scheduler automatically paused shedding and deferred defrag, preserving tail SLOs
results_summary: Mixed-harness p95 latency: baseline 228ms -> hybridizer 210ms (8% improvement)
KV effective hit-rate: baseline 0.71 -> hybridizer 0.69 (2.8% drop, within target)
GPU slab fragmentation metric (measured by freedable-slab fraction): baseline 0.22 -> after defrag 0.10 (reduction 12%)
CPU overhead: hybridization logic added ~1.8% CPU on coordinator hosts; acceptable for Dedicated nodes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Shedding may evict semantic prefixes that cause hallucination regressions. Mitigation: preserve high-value tokens by marking policy-stable prefixes (customer-annotated) and excluding from shedding pool
Risk: Defrag can increase PCIe activity and compete with model copies. Mitigation: throttle compaction bandwidth and prefer copy-on-idle windows; add circuit breaker if host IO spikes
Risk: Multi-tenant fairness: aggressive shedding could favor some tenants. Mitigation: scheduler uses tenant-weighted fairness buckets and tracks per-tenant eviction budget
